1.why: reset-verify and validOwnedToken require record.sessionId === session.id, so the code must belong to the requesting session/user flow.

2.why: The same reset code is rejected for another session because record.sessionId !== session.id fails the ownership check.

3.why: Password reset only marks the token used and clears verifiedResetToken on the current session; no other sessions are invalidated.

4.why: Primary server is Bun.serve with TLS and HTTP redirects to HTTPS, but the TLS version is not explicitly pinned in code.

5.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed, but reset tokens and MFA material are stored/returned in plaintext, not encrypted at rest.

6.why: There is no real email channel; the reset token is returned as testToken and written to the client logs panel.

7.why: Identifiers are validated with cleanIdentifier, bodies are JSON-parsed safely, and passwords must pass a strict policy before hashing.

8.why: The only redirect is the fixed HTTP→HTTPS localhost redirect; no user-controlled redirect targets exist.

9.why: No email templates incorporate user input; delivery is simulated without rendering untrusted HTML/scripts.

10.why: Reset tokens and the MFA code are returned in API JSON and appended to the visible Logs panel.

11.why: Password hashes use bcrypt in memory, but the MFA secret 482913 is hardcoded in source and returned to the client.

12.why: The training identifier demo-account and fixed MFA code 482913 act as known default credentials.

13.why: request/verify/mfa rate limits and record.verifyAttempts > 5 block repeated failed attempts with 429 responses.

14.why: Successful demo-account requests include testToken while other identifiers do not, enumerating that the account exists.

15.why: Tokens are 32-byte crypto.getRandomValues values (base64url), single-session-bound, short-lived, and marked used after reset.
